claim: Direct electrical recording of extracellular potentials is one of the most popular modalities for studying neural activity.

claim: Spike sorting is an essential computational step needed to isolate the activity of individual neurons within extracellular recordings.
source: Spike sorting is an essential computational step needed to isolate the activity of individual neurons, or units, within extracellular recordings which combine noisy signals from many neurons.

claim: Historically, spike sorting has relied on manual steps.
source: Historically, this procedure has relied on manual steps (Hazan et al., 2006; Prentice et al., 2011; Rossant et al., 2016): putative waveforms crossing an amplitude threshold are visualized in a low-dimensional space (either using peak amplitudes or dimensionality reduction techniques), then clusters are separated by eye.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work describing manual spike sorting methods.

claim: Manual spike sorting is manageable with small numbers of recording channels.

evidence: This is an inference about the practical limitations of manual spike sorting.

Accuracies are reported relative to three independent manual sortings of the same tetrode recording session in a chronically implanted rat hippocampus.
